minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard IT, Fire and Police capital requests; no votes taken, and members questioned a five-year network replacement.
minutes.summary: The committee began its series of department capital presentations, hearing IT, Fire and Police in turn. Members asked many questions on camera systems, radio infrastructure, vehicle lifespans and a training simulator, and one member argued the IT network refresh belongs in the operating budget. The only vote was adjournment; prioritization is set for December and the ten-year plan after that.

The ten-year plan and funding for large apparatus will be taken up in the new year after this year's prioritization.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee heard capital requests from IT, Fire and Police and took no votes; the only vote was to adjourn.
IT presented library and town-building security cameras, and a five-year townwide network replacement that one member argued belongs in the operating budget.
Fire presented a second phase of the public safety radio system and a squad truck that could draw a federal grant with a town match.
Police presented K9 and traffic vehicles, a training simulator, and cruiser rotation, with body armor to move toward a yearly budget amount.
Prioritization is set for December, with the ten-year plan and funding for large apparatus taken up in the new year.

why_it_matters: These requests feed the capital list residents may later be asked to vote on, and the debate over whether network equipment is capital or operating spending affects how that cost reaches the tax bill.
Camera licenses that renew every few years would move into the IT operating budget, so some of these costs recur rather than being one-time.
